title: Mason's lane is the executable/external layer, distributed via instruction files
body: Deep research (2026-07, 22 sources, adversarially verified): instruction files are the only harness mechanism with mass adoption (61-100% of 2,853 engineered repos vs <20% for everything else), AGENTS.md is converging bottom-up as the tool-agnostic standard, and the under-occupied surface vendors don't own is the executable/external layer — MCP servers, memory, and freshness infrastructure. Also: persistent memory is high-leverage ONLY with a quality pipeline (dedupe/verification/freshness), and sophisticated retrieval scaffolds don't beat simple baselines on code-derivable questions. Consequences: distribute through instruction files (kept ruthlessly concise), never compete with harness-native compaction/retrieval, and invest in the decision/drift/verify pipeline over Q&A navigation features.
